definition_en: the quality of being funny, or to go along with someone
core_image: 朋友围坐聊天，一个人说着趣事，众人微笑
scene: 他有一种温和的幽默感。 He has a gentle sense of humour.
sceneCN: 这里 humour 是「幽默」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他有一种温和的幽默感。

senses.title: The quality of being funny
senses.definition: the quality that makes something funny
senses.definitionCN: 使事物可笑的品质
senses.example: He has a gentle sense of humour.
senses.exampleCN: 他有一种温和的幽默感。
senses.why: This is the core sense of funniness.
senses.whyCN: 这是「幽默」的核心义项。

senses.title: A mood or temper
senses.definition: a state of mind, often a good one
senses.definitionCN: 心境，常指好心情
senses.example: She was in good humour after the walk.
senses.exampleCN: 散步之后她心情很好。
senses.why: This older sense survives in phrases about good or bad humour.
senses.whyCN: 这一较旧义项仍保留在表示心情好坏的短语中。

senses.title: To go along with someone
senses.definition: to accept someone's wishes to keep them happy
senses.definitionCN: 为让对方高兴而顺从其意愿
senses.example: We humoured the old man and listened.
senses.exampleCN: 我们迁就老人，听他说话。
senses.why: The verb keeps the idea of adjusting to a mood.
senses.whyCN: 动词义保留了顺应情绪的意思。

intro.en: Humour began as a word for moisture and the body fluids.
intro.cn: humour 最初指湿气与体液。

items.en: Humor meant moisture.
items.cn: humor 意为湿气。

items.en: Humor meant a bodily fluid.
items.cn: humor 意为体液。

items.en: Humour named a person's temperament.
items.cn: humour 指人的性情。

items.en: Humour came to mean funniness.
items.cn: humour 转而表示幽默。

items.en: Humour also means to indulge someone.
items.cn: humour 也表示迁就某人。

note.en: Humour is compared with look-alike words and with words for fun.
note.cn: 把 humour 与形近词以及表示趣味、玩笑的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Humour is both funniness and the mood that makes it possible.
normalIntro.cn: humour 既是幽默的品质，也是让幽默成为可能的心境。

normal.en: He has a gentle sense of humour.
normal.cn: 他有一种温和的幽默感。

normal.en: She was in good humour after the walk.
normal.cn: 散步之后她心情很好。

normal.en: We humoured the old man and listened.
normal.cn: 我们迁就老人，听他说话。

normal.en: His dry humour made everyone smile.
normal.cn: 他的冷幽默让每个人都笑了。

normal.en: It takes humour to laugh at your own mistakes.
normal.cn: 拿自己的错误开玩笑需要幽默感。

abstract.en: Humour is a mood and a method at once.
abstract.cn: 幽默既是心境，也是方法。

abstract.en: The word once meant fluid; laughter still flows.
abstract.cn: 这个词原指液体；笑声依然流动。

abstract.en: To humour someone is to bend without breaking.
abstract.cn: 迁就某人就是弯曲而不折断。

examples.en: He has a gentle sense of humour.
examples.cn: 他有一种温和的幽默感。

examples.en: She was in good humour after the walk.
examples.cn: 散步之后她心情很好。

examples.en: We humoured the old man and listened.
examples.cn: 我们迁就老人，听他说话。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 体液 → 性情 → 幽默
dict_mnemonic.text: humour 原指体液，古人认为体液决定性情，后来「性情」演变为「幽默」，也保留了「迁就某人心境」的动词义。

root: 源自拉丁语 humor（湿气、体液），中世纪认为体液影响性情，后由 temperament 引申为幽默。

sensesIntro.en: Humour means funniness, a mood, or the act of indulging someone.
sensesIntro.cn: humour 表示幽默、心境，或迁就某人。

core.en: A flow of mood and laughter.
core.cn: 情绪与笑声的流动。

branches.en: He has a gentle sense of humour.
branches.cn: 他有一种温和的幽默感。

branches.en: His dry humour made everyone smile.
branches.cn: 他的冷幽默让每个人都笑了。

branches.en: She was in good humour after the walk.
branches.cn: 散步之后她心情很好。

branches.en: We humoured the old man and listened.
branches.cn: 我们迁就老人，听他说话。

branches.en: A funny remark and a happy mood share one word.
branches.cn: 有趣的话与愉快的心情共用一个词。

intro.en: Humour forms humorous, humorist, and the verb humoured.
intro.cn: humour 可构成 humorous、humorist 以及动词形式 humoured。

latinIntro.en: The Latin humor also gave humid and humidity, which keep the old wet sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 humor 还催生了 humid 与 humidity，保留了古老的湿气含义。

items.exampleCN: 幽默作家写了一个专栏。
他作了毫无幽默感的回答。

latinEntries.example: Humor is the source of humour.
latinEntries.exampleCN: humor 是 humour 的来源。

definition_zh: 富有成效的；果实累累的
definition_en: producing good results, or bearing a lot of fruit
core_image: 果树枝头挂满果实，讨论也有了成果
scene: 那次讨论非常富有成效。 The discussion was very fruitful.
sceneCN: 这里 fruitful 是「富有成效的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：那次讨论非常富有成效。

senses.title: Producing good results
senses.definition: producing good or useful results
senses.definitionCN: 产生良好或有用的结果
senses.example: The discussion was very fruitful.
senses.exampleCN: 那次讨论非常富有成效。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常见的义项。

senses.title: Heavy with fruit
senses.definition: bearing a lot of fruit
senses.definitionCN: 结出大量果实的
senses.example: The old apple tree is still fruitful.
senses.exampleCN: 那棵老苹果树仍然果实累累。
senses.why: This keeps the literal picture behind the word.
senses.whyCN: 这保留了词背后字面上的画面。

senses.title: Richly productive
senses.definition: producing many good things, such as works or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 产生许多佳作或好想法的
senses.example: She had a fruitful career as a writer.
senses.exampleCN: 她的写作生涯硕果累累。
senses.why: The harvest image extends to creative work.
senses.whyCN: 收获的意象延伸到创作劳动。

intro.en: Fruitful joins fruit with the suffix -ful.
intro.cn: fruitful 由 fruit 加后缀 -ful 构成。

items.en: The suffix -full meant full of.
items.cn: 后缀 -full 意为充满……的。

items.en: Fruit entered English from Old French.
items.cn: fruit 从古法语进入英语。

items.en: Fruit and -ful combined as fruitful.
items.cn: fruit 与 -ful 组合成 fruitful。

items.en: The sense widened from trees to work.
items.cn: 词义从树木扩展到工作。

items.en: It now praises discussions and years.
items.cn: 如今它用来赞美讨论和年份。

note.en: Fruitful is compared with look-alike words and words for productivity.
note.cn: 把 fruitful 与形近词以及表示多产的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fruitful means full of fruit and full of results.
normalIntro.cn: fruitful 意为果实满满，也成果满满。

normal.en: The discussion was very fruitful.
normal.cn: 那次讨论非常富有成效。

normal.en: The old apple tree is still fruitful.
normal.cn: 那棵老苹果树仍然果实累累。

normal.en: She had a fruitful career as a writer.
normal.cn: 她的写作生涯硕果累累。

normal.en: They had a fruitful collaboration last year.
normal.cn: 他们去年合作富有成果。

normal.en: The rain made the valley fruitful.
normal.cn: 雨水让山谷变得多产。

abstract.en: A fruitful mind plants ideas that others can harvest.
abstract.cn: 富有成效的头脑种下别人也能收获的想法。

abstract.en: Time used well is always fruitful.
abstract.cn: 善加利用的时间总是有收获的。

abstract.en: Good questions make a meeting fruitful.
abstract.cn: 好的问题让会议富有成效。

examples.en: The discussion was very fruitful.
examples.cn: 那次讨论非常富有成效。

examples.en: The old apple tree is still fruitful.
examples.cn: 那棵老苹果树仍然果实累累。

examples.en: She had a fruitful career as a writer.
examples.cn: 她的写作生涯硕果累累。

dict_mnemonic.text: fruitful = fruit（果实）+ -ful（充满）；由「结满果实」引申为「富有成效」，与 fruitless（徒劳的）相对。

root: 由 fruit 加后缀 -ful（充满……的）构成；核心义「果实满满的」，引申为「成效丰硕」。

sensesIntro.en: Fruitful describes heavy branches, good results, or a productive life of work.
sensesIntro.cn: fruitful 形容果实压枝、结果良好，或创作多产。

core.en: Full of fruit, and therefore full of results.
core.cn: 结满果实，因而也成果丰硕。

branches.en: A talk yields useful decisions.
branches.cn: 一次谈话产生有用的决定。

branches.en: Branches bend under heavy fruit.
branches.cn: 枝条被沉甸甸的果实压弯。

branches.en: A writer's years produce many works.
branches.cn: 作家的岁月产生许多作品。

branches.en: Harvest and creative output share one image.
branches.cn: 收获与创作产出共享同一个意象。

branches.en: Good soil rewards patient care.
branches.cn: 好土壤回报耐心的照料。

intro.en: Fruitful shows how -ful turns a noun into a rich adjective.
intro.cn: fruitful 展示了 -ful 如何把名词变成含义丰富的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The suffix is Germanic; the root fruit came through French.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀属日耳曼语；词根 fruit 经法语传入。

items.meaningCN: 果实累累的；富有成效的

items.exampleCN: 他们一起工作卓有成效。

items.example: The fruitfulness of the soil surprised them.
items.exampleCN: 土地的肥沃让他们惊讶。
我们进行了一次富有成效的讨论。

items.example: The river made the land fruitful.
It was a fruitful year for the team.
items.exampleCN: 对团队来说那是成果丰硕的一年。
实验室做了富有成效的研究。

definition_en: a situation in which life is very difficult because of a lack of money or comfort
core_image: 一间漏风的屋子里只点着一支蜡烛
scene: 战争年代他们经历了许多困苦。 They faced great hardship during the war.
sceneCN: 这里 hardship 是「困苦」（第 1 个义项）；句意：战争年代他们经历了许多困苦。

senses.title: Difficult living conditions
senses.definition: conditions of life that are hard because of poverty or lack of comfort
senses.definitionCN: 因贫穷或缺乏舒适而艰难的生活条件
senses.example: They faced great hardship during the war.
senses.exampleCN: 战争年代他们经历了许多困苦。
senses.why: This is the main social sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最主要的社会义项。

senses.title: A hard experience
senses.definition: something difficult that a person has to go through
senses.definitionCN: 一个人不得不经历的难事
senses.example: Moving alone was a real hardship.
senses.exampleCN: 独自搬家真是件艰难的事。
senses.why: The state of difficulty is also counted one by one.
senses.whyCN: 艰难的状态，也能一件件数出来。

senses.title: Suffering
senses.definition: serious suffering caused by hard conditions
senses.definitionCN: 由艰苦条件造成的严重痛苦
senses.example: The book describes the hardships of the poor.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书描写了穷人的苦难。
senses.why: The plural names many separate troubles.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式指许多各自分开的苦处。

intro.en: Hardship is hard plus the noun ending -ship, which names a state or condition.
intro.cn: hardship 是 hard 加名词后缀 -ship，表示状态或处境。

items.en: Heard meant firm or severe.
items.cn: heard 意为坚实或严厉。

items.en: The ending -ship named a condition.
items.cn: 后缀 -ship 表示一种处境。

items.en: Hardship named a state of severe difficulty.
items.cn: hardship 指极为艰难的处境。

items.en: The word spread to money troubles.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到经济上的困难。

items.en: The plural named many separate troubles.
items.cn: 复数形式指许多具体的苦处。

note.en: Hardship is compared with look-alike words and with words for difficulty and suffering.
note.cn: 把 hardship 与形近词以及表示困难和痛苦的词作比较。

entries.definition: the state of being hard to do
great pain of body or mind
the state of being very poor

normalIntro.en: Hardship is hard turned into a condition of life, and then counted one by one.
normalIntro.cn: hardship 是「hard」变成的一种生活处境，然后被一件件数出来。

normal.en: They endured years of hardship.
normal.cn: 他们忍受了多年困苦。

normal.en: Economic hardship closed the factory.
normal.cn: 经济困难让工厂关了门。

normal.en: She never spoke of her hardships.
normal.cn: 她从不提自己受的苦。

normal.en: Hardship made the family closer.
normal.cn: 困苦让这家人更亲密。

normal.en: The scholarship helps students in hardship.
normal.cn: 这项奖学金帮助有困难的学生。

abstract.en: Hardship is a teacher no one invites.
abstract.cn: 困苦是没人邀请的老师。

abstract.en: A life without friction never learns its own shape.
abstract.cn: 没有摩擦的生活，永远不知道自己是什么形状。

abstract.en: What is endured quietly becomes strength later.
abstract.cn: 默默忍受的东西，日后会变成力量。

examples.en: They faced great hardship during the war.
examples.cn: 战争年代他们经历了许多困苦。

examples.en: Moving alone was a real hardship.
examples.cn: 独自搬家真是件艰难的事。

examples.en: The book describes the hardships of the poor.
examples.cn: 这本书描写了穷人的苦难。

dict_mnemonic.text: hardship 是 hard 加后缀 -ship（状态），指生活上的「困苦、艰难」；economic hardship 是经济困难，face hardship 是面对困苦，复数 hardships 指一桩桩具体的苦处。

root: hard（艰难的）加名词后缀 -ship（处境、状态）；指因贫穷或匮乏而艰难的生活状态，复数指具体的苦难。

sensesIntro.en: Hardship is hard living, a single hard experience, or many separate sufferings.
sensesIntro.cn: hardship 是艰难的生活、一次艰难的遭遇，或一桩桩苦难。

core.en: A room with a cold draft.
core.cn: 一间灌着冷风的屋子。

branches.en: A family eats thin soup for weeks.
branches.cn: 一家人连着几周喝稀汤。

branches.en: A young man carries his bags up six floors.
branches.cn: 一个年轻人提着行李爬六层楼。

branches.en: An old woman counts the winters she survived.
branches.cn: 老妇人数着她熬过的冬天。

branches.en: A hard condition becomes a hard memory.
branches.cn: 艰难的处境，变成艰难的记忆。

branches.en: Each single trouble becomes part of the whole suffering.
branches.cn: 一桩桩难处，汇成整体的苦难。

intro.en: Hardship is a mass noun with a countable plural for separate troubles.
intro.cn: hardship 是不可数名词，复数则指一桩桩具体的苦难。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.exampleCN: 困苦让他们变得有耐心。

items.example: He tested the hardness of the stone.
The fund helps families in financial hardship.
items.exampleCN: 该基金帮助有经济困难的家庭。

definition_zh: 介词；前置词；放在前面的事物；预先放置
definition_en: a word placed before a noun or pronoun to show its relation to another word, or, in rarer uses, something put in front or the act of placing it there
core_image: 一块小方木被摆到一列积木的最前面，箭头指着它与后面那块之间的缝隙
scene: 黑板上写着一行句子，老师用粉笔在其中一个短词下画了圈。 In the phrase at the station, at is a preposition.
sceneCN: 这里 preposition 是「介词」（第 1 个义项：置于名词之前、表示关系的虚词）；句意为在 at the station 这个短语中，at 就是介词。图中可辨识物件：黑板、粉笔圈、一列积木。

pos.zh: 介词；前置词；放在前面的事物

derivatives.zh: 由 preposition 加 -al 构成，义为「介词的；介词性的」
由 post-（在后）替换 prae- 构成，义为「后置词」
由 prepositional 加 -ly 构成，义为「以介词的方式」

senses.title: A function word set before a noun
senses.definition: a small word such as in, on or at, placed before a noun or pronoun to show place, time or another relation
senses.definitionCN: in、on、at 这类小词，放在名词或代词之前，表示处所、时间或其他关系
senses.example: In the phrase under the table, under is a preposition.
senses.exampleCN: 在 under the table 这个短语里，under 是介词。
senses.why: Latin praepositio named a placing in front, and grammarians applied it to the little word set before a noun, which is why the grammar term and the literal image are the same.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praepositio 指置于前方，语法学家用它来称呼置于名词前的小词，所以这个语法术语与字面画面本来就是同一件事。

senses.title: Something placed in front
senses.definition: a thing set at the front of something else, a literal sense now found mainly in learned or older writing
senses.definitionCN: 被放到另一事物最前面的东西，这一字面义如今多见于学术或较早的文字
senses.example: The title page serves as a preposition to the whole book.
senses.exampleCN: 扉页像是放在整本书前面的一件东西。
senses.why: The grammatical sense grew out of the literal one and never fully replaced it, so the word can still be used of any part put at the head of a whole.
senses.whyCN: 语法义是从字面义长出来的，却从未完全取代它，所以这个词仍可用来指任何被放在整体最前面的部分。

senses.title: To place something in advance
senses.definition: to put people or supplies in position ahead of the time they will be needed, chiefly in military writing
senses.definitionCN: 在需要之前就把人员或物资放到位置上，主要用于军事文字
senses.example: The crew prepositioned supplies along the route.
senses.exampleCN: 队员沿路线预先放置了补给。
senses.why: Modern military writing turned the noun into a verb, so to preposition is to do the placing ahead of time that the old noun merely named.
senses.whyCN: 现代军事文字把这个名词当动词用，于是 to preposition 就是去做那个旧名词所指的「提前摆好」的动作。

intro.en: Preposition is a Latin grammatical term built from a prefix of place and a verb of putting, and it reached English through French with the literal sense intact.
intro.cn: preposition 是一个由位置前缀与「放置」动词构成的拉丁语法术语，经法语进入英语时字面义仍然完好。

items.en: Ponere meant to put or to place, and it is the verb behind position, deposit and postpone.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置，是 position、deposit 与 postpone 等词背后的动词。

items.en: Prae- meant before, so praeponere meant to put one thing in front of another, and it could also mean to set a person over others.
items.cn: prae- 意为在前面，praeponere 便指把一物放到另一物之前，也可指把某人置于他人之上。

items.en: The noun praepositio named a placing in front, and Latin grammarians used it for the small word set before a noun.
items.cn: 名词 praepositio 指置于前方，拉丁语法学家用它来指置于名词前的小词。

items.en: Old French borrowed the term as preposicion, keeping both the grammatical and the literal sense.
items.cn: 古法语把该词借作 preposicion，同时保留语法义与字面义。

items.en: English settled on preposition, and the contrast with postposition keeps the idea of position visible in the word.
items.cn: 英语定型为 preposition，与 postposition 的对照让「位置」这层意思在词里一直看得见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin verb ponere, to place; the near-meaning group gathers the other small word classes that grammar sets beside it.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁动词 ponere（放置）上的形式；近义组收语法上与它并列的其他虚词类别。

entries.definition: Of or belonging to a preposition, as in a prepositional phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 由 preposition 加 -al 构成，义为介词的，如介词短语。

entries.definition: A word of the same kind but placed after its noun, the mirror image of a preposition.
entries.definitionCN: 同类的小词但放在名词之后，是介词的反向对应物。

entries.definition: The placing of one noun beside another to explain it, built on the same Latin verb ponere.
entries.definitionCN: 同位；把一个名词放在另一名词旁作解释，同样出自拉丁动词 ponere。

entries.definition: In a way that uses or functions as a preposition.
entries.definitionCN: 以介词的方式；起介词作用地。

entries.definition: A short uninflected word that works with a verb, such as up in look up.
entries.definitionCN: 小品词；与动词搭配的短小不变词，如 look up 中的 up。

entries.definition: A word such as and or because that joins words or clauses.
entries.definitionCN: 连词；连接词或从句的词，如 and、because。

entries.definition: The general term covering both prepositions and postpositions.
entries.definitionCN: 介词与后置词的统称，是语言类型学中的术语。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin noun of placing before, and its family keeps returning to position, order and what stands at the head of something else.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「置于前方」的名词，同族词反复回到位置、次序以及站在他物最前面的东西。

normal.en: Praepositio is prae- plus positio, a placing before, so the grammar term is simply the literal act applied to words.
normal.cn: praepositio 是 prae- 加 positio（放置），意为置于前方；语法术语不过是把这个字面动作用到词上。

normal.en: Its root ponere means to put, and the same root appears in position, deposit and postpone.
normal.cn: 它的词根 ponere 意为放置，position、deposit、postpone 都出同一词根。

normal.en: Postposition swaps the prefix for post- and names the mirror case, a word placed after its noun.
normal.cn: postposition 把前缀换成 post-，指相反的情形：放在名词之后的词。

normal.en: Prepositional adds -al and turns the noun into an adjective for phrases and uses.
normal.cn: prepositional 加 -al，把名词变成形容短语与用法的形容词。

normal.en: The rare verb to preposition keeps the old image: put things in place before they are needed.
normal.cn: 罕用的动词 to preposition 保留了旧画面：在需要之前就把东西放到位。

abstract.en: A preposition is a word that refuses to stand alone; it exists to point at a relation between two others.
abstract.cn: 介词是一个不肯独自站立的词，它存在的意义是指出另外两者之间的关系。

abstract.en: Grammar and ordinary speech share the same picture here: something small is put in front, and the whole sentence leans on it.
abstract.cn: 语法与日常说法在这里共用一幅画面：一个小东西被放到前面，整句都倚靠着它。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that position is meaning, since moving it changes what the sentence says.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒人：位置本身就是意义，挪动它，句子所说的东西就变了。

examples.en: In the phrase under the table, under is a preposition.
examples.cn: 在 under the table 这个短语里，under 是介词。

examples.en: The title page serves as a preposition to the whole book.
examples.cn: 扉页像是放在整本书前面的一件东西。

examples.en: The crew prepositioned supplies along the route.
examples.cn: 队员沿路线预先放置了补给。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑瑞坡基申」——先扑到前面占好位置；preposition 就是放在前面的词，即介词。

root: 源自拉丁语 praepositio（置于前方），由 prae-（在前）与 ponere（放置）构成的 praeponere 派生，经古法语 preposicion 进入英语；与 position、postpone 同出 ponere，与 prepare 的 parare（使就绪）不是同一条线。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something placed in front; the senses divide into the grammatical word set before a noun, the literal thing put at the head, and the rare act of placing in advance.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被放到前面的东西；义项由此分出置于名词前的语法虚词、字面上放在最前面的物件，以及罕用的「预先放置」动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small block moved to the front of a row of blocks, an arrow pointing at the gap behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块小方木被摆到一列积木的最前面，箭头指着它与后面那块之间的缝隙。

branches.en: a circled word standing just before a noun

branches.cn: 小路起点竖起的标柱

branches.cn: 岔路口前竖立的指路牌

branches.en: a label fixed to a jar before it is filled
branches.cn: 装罐之前就贴好的标签

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix of place, a verb of putting and a noun suffix, and the same pieces build its grammar relatives.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀、表示「放置」的动词与名词后缀组成，同样的部件也造出它的语法同族词。

latinIntro.en: Preposition goes back to Latin praepositio, from prae- and ponere, to place; praeponere and positio carry the same pieces.
latinIntro.cn: preposition 上溯拉丁语 praepositio，由 prae- 与 ponere（放置）构成；praeponere 与 positio 用的是同样的部件。

definition_en: lasting too long and therefore boring
core_image: 一页页重复的表格铺满桌面
scene: 那份报告冗长乏味，读到一半他就走神了。 The report was so tedious that he lost focus halfway through.
sceneCN: 这里 tedious 是「冗长乏味的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：那份报告冗长乏味，读到一半他就走神了。

senses.title: Long and boring
senses.definition: continuing for so long that it becomes boring
senses.definitionCN: 持续太久而让人感到无聊的
senses.example: The report was so tedious that he lost focus halfway through.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告冗长乏味，读到一半他就走神了。
senses.why: The Latin root means weariness, so the word describes what causes that tiredness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为疲倦，这个词形容的正是让人疲倦的东西。

senses.title: Slow and tiring
senses.definition: moving so slowly that it exhausts patience
senses.definitionCN: 慢得让人耗尽耐心的
senses.example: The tedious traffic made the trip feel endless.
senses.exampleCN: 缓慢拥挤的交通让这趟路显得没有尽头。
senses.why: Weariness also comes from things that crawl rather than run.
senses.whyCN: 疲倦感也来自那些慢得像爬的东西，而不只是长。

intro.en: Tedious comes from the Latin word for weariness.
intro.cn: tedious 来自拉丁语中表示疲倦的词。

items.en: Taedium meant weariness and disgust.
items.cn: taedium 意为疲倦与厌烦。

items.en: Taediosus meant causing weariness.
items.cn: taediosus 意为令人疲倦的。

items.en: Tedieux carried the sense of boring.
items.cn: tedieux 表示令人厌烦。

items.en: Tedious entered English for dull, long things.
items.cn: tedious 进入英语，形容冗长沉闷之物。

items.en: It now describes work, speech, and waiting.
items.cn: 如今它形容工作、讲话与等待。

note.en: Tedious is compared with look-alike forms and with adjectives of boredom.
note.cn: 把 tedious 与形近形式以及表示无聊的形容词作对比。

normalIntro.en: Tedious names the tiredness that long, flat things produce.
normalIntro.cn: tedious 指的是冗长平淡之物带来的疲倦。

normal.en: The report was tedious and long.
normal.cn: 这份报告冗长乏味。

normal.en: Copying the list was tedious work.
normal.cn: 抄写清单是件乏味的工作。

normal.en: The speech felt tedious to everyone.
normal.cn: 这场讲话让所有人都觉得沉闷。

normal.en: Tedious details slowed the meeting.

normal.en: The traffic made the drive tedious.
normal.cn: 交通状况让这趟车开得很累人。

abstract.en: Boredom is weariness with a schedule.
abstract.cn: 无聊是对重复日程的疲倦。

abstract.en: Even a short wait can feel tedious.

root: 拉丁语 taedium（疲倦、厌烦）经 taediosus 与法语 tedieux 进入英语，指令人疲倦的冗长。

sensesIntro.en: Tedious describes what wears patience out, whether by length or by slowness.
sensesIntro.cn: tedious 形容把耐心磨掉的东西，无论靠长度还是靠缓慢。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: endless identical rows on a page.

branches.en: Length and repetition create boredom.
branches.cn: 长度与重复制造无聊。

branches.en: Slowness wears patience out too.
branches.cn: 缓慢同样磨掉耐心。

branches.cn: 两者都归于同一种疲倦。

branches.en: Reports and speeches are typical.
branches.cn: 报告与演讲是典型场景。

branches.en: Traffic is tedious without being long.
branches.cn: 交通未必长，却一样乏味。

intro.en: Tedious has a small family built on tedium.

latinIntro.en: Latin taedium, weariness, is the direct source.

definition_en: a very holy person honored by a religion; a very kind and patient person; a title before a holy name

senses.title: A holy person

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a haloed figure in a church window.

branches.en: The base sense is a holy person.

definition_en: a movement of the body that expresses meaning, or a symbolic act

senses.title: Movement of the body
senses.definition: a movement of the hands or body that shows meaning
senses.definitionCN: 手或身体的、表达含义的动作
senses.example: He made a gesture towards the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝门口做了个手势。
senses.why: The Latin source names the carrying of the body, then a movement of it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源先指身体的姿态，后指身体的动作。

senses.title: Symbolic act

senses.definitionCN: 表达某种态度或感情的行为

senses.why: A small act can carry a message as clearly as a hand does.
senses.whyCN: 一个小举动可以像手势一样清楚地传递信息。

senses.title: To signal with the body

senses.example: She gestured for us to sit down.
senses.exampleCN: 她示意我们坐下。
senses.why: The noun became a verb naming the act of making a sign.

definition_en: at a time later than an event, especially in the sequence of a narrative
core_image: 雨停之后，屋檐还在一滴一滴地落水
scene: 会议在十点结束，大家陆续走出大楼。 We went for coffee afterward.

senses.title: At a later time
senses.definition: at a time following an event that has just been mentioned

senses.exampleCN: 会后我们去喝了咖啡。

pos.zh: 动词：管理；实施；给予；主持

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「管理；行政部门」
由动词词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「行政的；管理的」
由动词加表人后缀构成，义为「管理者；行政人员」
由名词逆构而成的动词，义为「管理；执行」

senses.title: To manage the running of an organization
senses.definition: to be in charge of the daily work, money or affairs of an institution
senses.definitionCN: 负责某个机构的日常工作、资金或事务
senses.example: She administers a team of forty nurses.
senses.exampleCN: 她管理着一支四十人的护士队伍。
senses.why: Latin minister meant a servant, and administrare meant to serve or manage affairs for someone, so the word still carries the idea of handling business on another's behalf.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minister 指仆人，administrare 意为「为他人服务、替人理事」，所以这个词至今带着「代他人打理事务」的意思。

senses.title: To give a drug or treatment
senses.definition: to give a medicine, treatment or form of help to a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 把药物、治疗或帮助给予人或动物
senses.example: Nurses administer the vaccine at the school clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在学校医务室接种疫苗。
senses.why: Serving someone came to include handing them what they need; medicine fixed the pattern as administer a drug.
senses.whyCN: 「服务他人」这一层引申出「把所需之物递到对方手上」，医学把这个搭配固定为 administer a drug。

senses.title: To put law or justice into effect
senses.definition: to carry out a law, a system or a form of justice in practice
senses.definitionCN: 在实际中执行法律、制度或某种公正
senses.example: The court administers justice without favour.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭执法不偏不倚。
senses.why: Managing affairs includes running the machinery of law, so the word came to name the act of making justice operate.
senses.whyCN: 管理事务也包括让法律机器运转，于是这个词被用来指「让公正真正生效」的动作。

senses.title: To lead a formal ceremony
senses.definition: to conduct a formal act such as an oath or a sacrament
senses.definitionCN: 主持宣誓、圣礼等正式仪式
senses.example: The judge administered the oath to the new citizens.
senses.exampleCN: 法官主持了新公民的宣誓仪式。
senses.why: A ceremony is also an affair to be managed; the one who serves it along is the one who administers it.
senses.whyCN: 仪式同样是一件需要料理的事务；把它一步步走完的人，就是在 administer 它。

intro.en: A Latin verb of serving grew into the vocabulary of management.
intro.cn: 一个表示「服务」的拉丁动词，长成了管理领域的词汇。

items.en: minister meant a servant or attendant, one who waits on another.
items.cn: minister 指仆人、随从，即服侍他人的人。

items.en: ministrare meant to serve, to wait on, and later to supply or furnish.
items.cn: ministrare 意为服侍、伺候，后来也指供给、提供。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus ministrare formed administrare, to serve, to manage affairs for someone.
items.cn: ad-（向）加 ministrare 构成 administrare，意为「服务、替人管理事务」。

items.en: Old French administrer narrowed the sense towards managing business or property.
items.cn: 古法语 administrer 把词义收窄到管理事务或财产。

items.en: English took the verb in the fifteenth century, first for managing affairs, later for giving medicine and law.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入该动词，先指管理事务，后来才用于给药与执法。

note.en: The first group is the minister family; the second gathers verbs of running, giving and enforcing.
note.cn: 第一组是 minister 词族；第二组收「管理」「给予」「执行」三类动词。

entries.definition: the work of managing an institution
to be in charge of something
to give out medicine or supplies
to make people obey a law

normalIntro.en: Inside the word sits minister, a servant.
normalIntro.cn: 词里藏着 minister，也就是「仆人」。

normal.en: administrare meant to serve, so to administer is to take care of affairs for others.
normal.cn: administrare 意为服务，所以 administer 是替别人照料事务。

normal.en: The same stem yields administration, administrator and administrative.
normal.cn: 同一词干生出 administration、administrator 与 administrative。

normal.en: Medicine fixed the phrase administer a drug.
normal.cn: 医学固定了 administer a drug（给药）这一说法。

normal.en: Law fixed the phrase administer justice.
normal.cn: 法律固定了 administer justice（执法）这一说法。

normal.en: Note the -ister ending, as in minister and register.
normal.cn: 注意词尾是 -ister，与 minister、register 相同。

abstract.en: See a steward carrying accounts in one hand and a tray in the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一位管家一手拿账本，一手端托盘。

abstract.en: Picture a nurse checking a dose twice before handing it over.
abstract.cn: 想象护士把剂量核对两遍才递出去。

abstract.en: Think of a judge making the law actually work in a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 想象法官让法律在法庭里真正运转起来。

examples.en: Nurses administer the vaccine at the school clinic.
examples.cn: 护士在学校医务室接种疫苗。

examples.en: The court administers justice without favour.
examples.cn: 法庭执法不偏不倚。

examples.en: He administered the fund for twenty years.
examples.cn: 他管理这笔基金二十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的米尼斯特」——额头上写着米尼斯特的名字，因为他是替大家管事的管家。

root: 拉丁语 administrare（服务、理事），由 ad-（向）与 ministrare（服侍）构成，词根 minister 意为「仆人」；本义「替人打理事务」，后引申为给药与执法。

sensesIntro.en: One verb of serving covers budgets, medicines, courts and ceremonies.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「服务」动词，管着预算、药物、法庭与仪式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steward handling affairs on someone else's behalf.
core.cn: 核心意象：管家替他人料理事务。

branches.en: a director running a small hospital
branches.cn: 院长打理一家小医院

branches.en: a nurse handing over a dose
branches.cn: 护士把药递到病人手上

branches.en: a court making justice operate
branches.cn: 法庭让公正得以施行

branches.en: a judge leading an oath
branches.cn: 法官主持宣誓

branches.en: handing over what the rule or the body requires
branches.cn: 把规则或身体所需之物交付出去

intro.en: A prefix of direction and a root of serving.
intro.cn: 一个表示方向的词头，加一个表示「服侍」的词根。

latinIntro.en: minister also gives ministry and ministerial.
latinIntro.cn: minister 还生出 ministry 与 ministerial。

definition_zh: 彻底的；全面的；仔细的；彻头彻尾的
definition_en: done completely, with every part attended to and nothing left out
core_image: 把抽屉整个抽出来翻到底：一件东西都不放过
scene: 海关的探员把行李箱翻了个底朝天,连衬里都摸过。 The officer gave the suitcase a thorough search before returning it.
sceneCN: 这里 thorough 是「彻底的」（第 1 个义项：每个细节都检查到）；句意：关员把行李箱彻底搜查了一遍才归还。

derivatives.zh: 彻底地；非常（thorough 加副词后缀 -ly）
彻底；周密（thorough 加名词后缀 -ness）
大道；通路（thorough 加 fare 复合，指通行之路）
穿过；通过（与 thorough 同源近亲，易混词）

senses.title: Complete, missing nothing
senses.definition: including every possible part or detail, with nothing missed
senses.definitionCN: 涵盖每个可能的部位或细节，无所遗漏
senses.example: The doctor carried out a thorough examination.
senses.exampleCN: 医生做了全面检查。
senses.why: The word sees the job as a road: a thorough job is one that has gone all the way through.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把工作看作一条路：彻底的工作就是把路走穿到底的工作。

senses.title: Careful and painstaking
senses.definition: taking care to do things properly and in detail, of a person or their manner
senses.definitionCN: 指人或其作风认真细致，务必做好每个环节
senses.example: She is thorough in everything she signs.
senses.exampleCN: 她签每份文件都一丝不苟。
senses.why: A person can inherit the road image: someone whose attention walks every step of the way.
senses.whyCN: 人也能继承道路意象：其注意力走完路上的每一步。

senses.title: Out-and-out, complete in kind
senses.definition: complete or absolute in kind, often of an undesirable quality
senses.definitionCN: 在性质上完全的、绝对的，常指不好的品质
senses.example: The scheme was a thorough failure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划彻底失败了。
senses.why: Completeness does not judge: if a thing fails through and through, thorough reports the depth of it.
senses.whyCN: 彻底不问好坏：一件事从头败到尾，thorough 报告的只是失败的深度。

intro.en: Thorough is the adjective twin of through: the same old word for moving from one side to the other, split by spelling into a preposition of motion and an adjective of completeness.
intro.cn: thorough 是 through 的形容词孪生兄弟：同一个表示「从一侧到另一侧」的古词，经拼写分化为表运动的介词与表彻底的形容词。

items.en: The root Thurh (or Thurh) meant through, from one side to the other, built on old words for door or passage.
items.cn: 词根 Thurh (or Thurh) 意为「穿过」，从一侧到另一侧，出自表示「门、通道」的古词。

items.en: Old English Thurh (or Thurh) worked as preposition and adverb, and the compound Thurhborh (or Thyrhborh) meant going right through, hence complete.
items.cn: 古英语 Thurh (or Thurh) 兼作介词与副词，复合词 Thurhborh (or Thyrhborh) 意为「直贯而过」，引申为完全。

items.en: Middle English split the spellings: through kept the motion job, and thorough took the completeness job.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写分化：through 保留运动义，thorough 接管彻底义。

items.en: The compound thoroughfare named a road that goes through, first for people, later for traffic.
items.cn: 复合词 thoroughfare 指可以贯穿而过的路，先指人行，后指车马。

items.en: Modern English settled the pair, and thorough became the standard word for complete care in work, study and examination.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了这对词，thorough 成为工作、学习、检查中「彻底用心」的标准词。

note.en: The first group separates the thorough-through spelling pair; the second compares words of completeness and care.
note.cn: 第一组区分 thorough 与 through 的拼写纠缠；第二组比较表示彻底与用心的词。

entries.definition: from one side to the other; the motion twin of thorough
entries.definitionCN: 穿过；通过（thorough 的运动义孪生词）

entries.definition: a public road that passes through a place
although; one letter from through and often mistyped for thorough
entries.definitionCN: 虽然；拼写与 through 一字之差，常与 thorough 误输

entries.definition: paying great attention to small details
entries.definitionCN: 一丝不苟的；对细节极为用心
穷尽的；涵盖一切可能的

normalIntro.en: Real hooks: the through twin, the road image inside the word, and the thoroughfare compound.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：through 孪生词、词内的道路意象、以及 thoroughfare 复合词。

normal.en: Thorough is through wearing an adjective's coat.
normal.cn: thorough 是穿上形容词外衣的 through。

normal.en: A thorough search goes through everything.
normal.cn: 彻底的搜查会把每样东西都翻 through。

normal.en: A thoroughfare is a road that goes through a town.
normal.cn: thoroughfare 是穿过城镇的路。

normal.en: Though, through, thorough: three spellings that trip every learner.
normal.cn: though、through、thorough：绊倒每个学习者的三种拼法。

normal.en: A thorough failure fails through and through.
normal.cn: 彻底的失败是从头到尾都失败。

abstract.en: Thorough is motion that refuses to stop halfway.
abstract.cn: thorough 是拒绝半途而废的运动。

abstract.en: Care that walks the whole road is called thorough.
abstract.cn: 走完整条路的用心，名为彻底。

abstract.en: Nothing thorough is ever done by halves.
abstract.cn: 彻底之事从无半途。

examples.en: Give the kitchen a thorough cleaning before the holiday.
examples.cn: 节日前把厨房彻底打扫一遍。

examples.en: The report is thorough, every figure checked twice.
examples.cn: 报告很周密，每个数字都核对了两遍。

examples.en: Their victory was a thorough one.
examples.cn: 他们的胜利是彻头彻尾的胜利。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟若」——彻底检查,连一「丝」缝隙都「若」在眼前 → thorough 彻底的

root: 与 through 同源的孪生词：日耳曼词根 Thurh (or Thurh)「贯穿」→ 古英语复合词「直贯而过」引申「完全」→ 中古英语拼写分化：through 表运动，thorough 表彻底。

sensesIntro.en: Thorough takes the road image of through and turns it into completeness: the job gone all the way, the person who walks every step, the failure through and through.
sensesIntro.cn: thorough 把 through 的道路意象转化为彻底：走到底的工作、走满每一步的人、彻头彻尾的失败。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road walked from gate to gate without a shortcut.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从大门走到尽头、绝不抄近路的路。

branches.en: The complete job, nothing skipped.
branches.cn: 完整的工作，无一遗漏。

branches.en: The person whose care walks every step.
branches.cn: 用心走满每一步的人。

branches.en: Depth of a quality, good or bad.
branches.cn: 性质的深度，无论好坏。

branches.en: Both keep the road: one for the task, one for the walker.
branches.cn: 两者都保留道路：一个给任务，一个给行人。

branches.en: Completeness applied to failure doubles its weight.
branches.cn: 彻底用于失败，分量加倍。

intro.en: Thorough carries native endings lightly: -ly and -ness, plus the old compound thoroughfare.
intro.cn: thorough 轻装佩挂本土词尾：-ly 与 -ness，外加古老的复合词 thoroughfare。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source; the word is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源；本词为日耳曼本土，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: a public road through a place
items.example: Oxford Street is a busy thoroughfare.
items.exampleCN: 牛津街是一条繁忙的大道。

items.meaning: from one side to the other

items.example: The theme runs throughout the novel.
items.exampleCN: 这一主题贯穿整部小说。
一丝不苟的笔记是他工作的印记。

items.meaningCN: 体贴的；深思的（读音对照）
items.example: A thoughtful reply ended the argument.
items.exampleCN: 一番体贴的回应结束了争执。

definition_en: to finish a task, or to bring about a result through effort
core_image: 最后一盏测试灯由红转绿，整块看板亮起完成
scene: 团队连续加班三周，终于把整套系统交付上线。 They accomplished the task two days early.
sceneCN: 这里的 accomplish 指「完成」（第 2 个义项：把承担的事情做到完结）；句意是他们提前两天完成了任务。

derivatives.zh: 义为「技艺高超的；有造诣的」

senses.title: To produce a result
senses.definition: brings about a result by effort
senses.definitionCN: 通过努力带来某种结果
senses.example: She accomplished a great deal in her first year.
senses.exampleCN: 她在第一年就取得了很大成绩。
senses.why: The Old French verb acomplir meant to fill up completely, and a result is what fills the space that effort was aimed at.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词 acomplir 意为「完全填满」，而努力的成果正是把原先瞄准的那块空白填满。

senses.title: To finish a task
senses.definition: brings a piece of work to its end
senses.definitionCN: 把一项工作做到终点
senses.example: They accomplished the task two days early.
senses.exampleCN: 他们提前两天完成了任务。
senses.why: Something filled up is also something finished, so the same verb names the closing of a task.
senses.whyCN: 被填满的东西也是被做完的东西，于是同一个动词也用来指任务的收尾。

intro.en: The word comes from a French verb meaning to complete or fill up.
intro.cn: 这个词来自一个意为「完成、填满」的法语动词。

items.en: complere meant to fill up completely.
items.cn: complere 意为完全填满。

items.en: ad- added the idea of bringing something towards its end.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 加入「把某事推向终点」的意思。

items.en: acomplir meant to carry something through to the end.
items.cn: acomplir 意为把某事做到底。

items.en: accomplish entered English as a verb of finishing work.
items.cn: accomplish 进入英语时，是表示「做完工作」的动词。

items.en: the word widened to cover achievements and skills.
items.cn: 后来它的范围扩大到成就与技艺。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accomplish family; the near-meaning group names finishing and achieving.
note.cn: 形近组是 accomplish 词族；近义组表示完成与达成。

entries.definition: to reach a goal after effort
to carry out a promise or aim

normalIntro.en: These hints follow complere, the Latin verb for filling up.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条贴着拉丁语里表示「填满」的 complere。

normal.en: complere is to fill, and a task is a space you fill with work.
normal.cn: complere 是填满，任务就是一块用工作填满的空间。

normal.en: the double c in the middle comes from the Latin picture of filling something up.
normal.cn: 中间的两个 c 来自拉丁语「把东西填满」的画面。

normal.en: to accomplish a goal is to leave no part of it empty.
normal.cn: 实现目标，就是不让它哪一块还空着。

normal.en: to accomplish a task is to put the last piece in place.
normal.cn: 完成任务，就是把最后一块放到位。

normal.en: an accomplished musician has filled years with practice.
normal.cn: 有造诣的音乐家，是用练习填满了许多年。

abstract.en: Picture a progress bar reaching the far edge.
abstract.cn: 想象进度条顶到最右边。

abstract.en: See the last green light come on across a control board.
abstract.cn: 想象整块控制板上最后一盏绿灯亮起。

abstract.en: Think of a jar filled to the brim with grain.
abstract.cn: 想象一只罐子被谷物填到罐口。

examples.en: They accomplished the task two days early.
examples.cn: 他们提前两天完成了任务。

examples.en: She accomplished a great deal in her first year.
examples.cn: 她在第一年就取得了很大成绩。

examples.en: We accomplished more than we had planned.
examples.cn: 我们完成的工作比计划的多。

dict_mnemonic.text: ac-（朝向）+ compl（填满）——把任务这块空地填满，就是 accomplish。

root: 古法语 acomplir（完成），源自拉丁语 complere（填满），加 ad- 表示推向终点，本义「填满、做到底」，引申为取得成果。

sensesIntro.en: One verb of filling up covers both the result gained and the task closed.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个表示「填满」的动词，既管得到的成果，也管收尾的任务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a progress bar reaching the far edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：进度条顶到最右边。

branches.en: a year of work leaving visible results
branches.cn: 一年工作留下看得见的成果

branches.en: a task closed two days before the deadline
branches.cn: 在截止前两天收尾的任务

branches.en: an aim reached with nothing left out
branches.cn: 没有缺项地达成目标

branches.en: the last piece set into place
branches.cn: 最后一块被放入原位

branches.en: what is finished is also what has been gained
branches.cn: 做完的事，也就是得到的东西

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix, a root for filling, and a verb ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁前缀、表示「填满」的词根与动词词尾组成。

latinIntro.en: The root plere, to fill, also gives complete, supplement and plenty.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 plere（填满）还给出 complete、supplement 与 plenty。

definition_en: coming after the forty-ninth, or one of fifty equal parts
core_image: 礼堂墙上挂起金色的「50」，彩带一路垂到地面
scene: 礼堂墙上挂起金色的五十，彩带一路垂到地面。 They celebrated their fiftieth anniversary.
sceneCN: 这里 fiftieth 是「第五十」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们庆祝了五十周年纪念。

senses.title: Ordinal fifty
senses.definition: coming after the forty-ninth in order
senses.definitionCN: 在顺序上位于第四十九之后
senses.example: They celebrated their fiftieth anniversary.
senses.exampleCN: 他们庆祝了五十周年纪念。
senses.why: This is the ordering sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示顺序的义项。

senses.title: One of fifty parts
senses.definition: one of fifty equal parts of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物被均分成五十份中的一份
senses.example: A fiftieth of the profit went to charity.
senses.exampleCN: 利润的五十分之一捐给了慈善机构。
senses.why: Ordinals also express fractions.
senses.whyCN: 序数词也用来表达分数。

intro.en: Fiftieth is the ordinal of fifty, from Old English fiftig and the suffix -th.
intro.cn: fiftieth 是 fifty 的序数形式，源自古英语 fiftig 加后缀 -th。

items.en: Fiftig meant fifty.
items.cn: fiftig 意为五十。

items.en: A suffix marked the ordinal form.
items.cn: 后缀用来标记序数形式。

items.en: The form shifted toward fiftieth.
items.cn: 词形逐渐演变为 fiftieth。

items.en: The spelling became standard.
items.cn: 拼写成为标准形式。

items.en: It named anniversaries and fractions.
items.cn: 它用来指周年纪念与分数。

note.en: Fiftieth is compared with similar-looking ordinals and with nearby numbers.
note.cn: 把 fiftieth 与形近序数词以及相邻数字作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fiftieth marks position fifty or one part in fifty.
normalIntro.cn: fiftieth 表示第五十位，或五十分之一。

normal.en: Add -th to fifty to get fiftieth.
normal.cn: fifty 加 -th 就是 fiftieth。

normal.en: A fiftieth anniversary marks fifty years.
normal.cn: 五十周年纪念标志五十年的历程。

normal.en: One fiftieth is two percent.
normal.cn: 五十分之一是百分之二。

normal.en: The fiftieth state means the last state to join.
normal.cn: the fiftieth state 指最后加入的州。

normal.en: Fiftieth is both ordinal and fraction.
normal.cn: fiftieth 既是序数词也是分数词。

abstract.en: Fifty years is long enough to become a story.
abstract.cn: 五十年长到足以变成一个故事。

abstract.en: The fiftieth part is small but still counted.
abstract.cn: 五十分之一很小，却仍被计算。

abstract.en: Anniversaries measure time by what survived.
abstract.cn: 周年纪念用「留下来什么」来丈量时间。

examples.en: They celebrated their fiftieth anniversary.
examples.cn: 他们庆祝了五十周年纪念。

examples.en: A fiftieth of the profit went to charity.
examples.cn: 利润的五十分之一捐给了慈善机构。

examples.en: The runner finished fiftieth overall.
examples.cn: 这位跑者总排名第五十。

dict_mnemonic.text: fiftieth 由基数词 fifty 加序数后缀 -th 构成，表示第五十，也用作分数「五十分之一」。

root: 由 fifty（五十）加序数后缀 -th 构成，核心义「排在第五十位的」。

sensesIntro.en: Fiftieth means the fiftieth in order or one of fifty equal parts.
sensesIntro.cn: fiftieth 意为第五十或五十分之一。

core.en: The position fifty in an ordered line.
core.cn: 有序排列中的第五十位。

branches.en: The fiftieth item in a series.
branches.cn: 序列中的第五十项。

branches.en: A single slice of fifty.
branches.cn: 五十份中的一份。

branches.en: A fiftieth year or anniversary.
branches.cn: 第五十年或五十周年。

branches.en: Position and portion share one form.
branches.cn: 位置与份额共用一个形式。

branches.en: One fiftieth is two percent.
branches.cn: 五十分之一是百分之二。

intro.en: Fiftieth belongs to the five and ten number family.
intro.cn: fiftieth 属于五与十的数词家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin quinquagesimus is the historical equivalent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quinquagesimus 是对应的历史形式。

items.exampleCN: 第五十点，名单到此结束。

items.meaning: the years from fifty to fifty-nine or the 1950s
items.example: He wrote the song in the fifties.
items.exampleCN: 他在五十年代写了这首歌。

definition_en: thin in an attractive way, or small in amount
core_image: 纤细的身影站在窗边，姿态从容
scene: 她身材苗条，走路却很稳。 She has a slender figure but walks steadily.
sceneCN: 这里 slender 是「苗条的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她身材苗条，走路却很稳。

senses.title: Thin and graceful
senses.definition: thin in a graceful and attractive way
senses.definitionCN: 以优雅好看的方式显得瘦
senses.example: She has a slender figure but walks steadily.
senses.exampleCN: 她身材苗条，走路却很稳。
senses.why: This is the everyday body sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常描述身材的义项。

senses.title: Small in amount
senses.definition: small in amount or degree, often too small
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度小，常指小得不足
senses.example: They won by a slender majority.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以微弱多数获胜。
senses.why: The thin image extends to small margins.
senses.whyCN: 「细」的意象延伸到微小的差距。

senses.title: Long and thin
senses.definition: long and thin in shape
senses.definitionCN: 形状又长又细
senses.example: Her slender fingers turned the page.
senses.exampleCN: 她纤细的手指翻过书页。
senses.why: Objects, not only bodies, can be slender.
senses.whyCN: 不仅身体，物体也可以是细长的。

intro.en: Slender is a Middle English word of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: slender 是中古英语词，来源不确定。

items.en: Slendre described something thin or small.
items.cn: slendre 描述细或小的东西。

items.en: The spelling became slender.
items.cn: 拼写演变为 slender。

items.en: It praised graceful thinness.
items.cn: 它用来赞美优雅的纤细。

items.en: It also described small chances and margins.
items.cn: 它也描述微小的机会和差距。

items.en: It spread to long thin objects.
items.cn: 词义扩展到细长的物体。

note.en: Slender is compared with look-alike words and words for thinness.
note.cn: 把 slender 与形近词以及表示纤细的词作比较。

entries.definition: a false spoken statement harming someone

normalIntro.en: Slender is thinness with grace, or a margin that is almost too small.
normalIntro.cn: slender 是优雅的纤细，或小得几乎不够的差距。

normal.en: She has a slender figure but walks steadily.
normal.cn: 她身材苗条，走路却很稳。

normal.en: They won by a slender majority.
normal.cn: 他们以微弱多数获胜。

normal.en: Her slender fingers turned the page.
normal.cn: 她纤细的手指翻过书页。

normal.en: There is only a slender chance of rain.
normal.cn: 下雨的机会很渺茫。

normal.en: A slender tree grew by the wall.
normal.cn: 墙边长着一棵细长的树。

abstract.en: A slender chance is still a chance.
abstract.cn: 微小的机会仍然是机会。

abstract.en: Strength does not always look broad.
abstract.cn: 力量并不总是显得宽厚。

abstract.en: Thin lines can hold a whole design.
abstract.cn: 细线也能撑起整个设计。

examples.en: She has a slender figure but walks steadily.
examples.cn: 她身材苗条，走路却很稳。

examples.en: They won by a slender majority.
examples.cn: 他们以微弱多数获胜。

examples.en: Her slender fingers turned the page.
examples.cn: 她纤细的手指翻过书页。

dict_mnemonic.text: slender 与 tender、slander 形近；a slender chance 是「渺茫的机会」，a slender majority 是「微弱多数」。

root: 中古英语 slendre，来源不确定；核心义「细而优雅」，引申为「微小、微薄」。

sensesIntro.en: Slender describes a graceful thin body, a small amount, or a long thin shape.
sensesIntro.cn: slender 形容优雅纤细的身材、微小的数量，或细长的形状。

core.en: Thinness with grace, or a margin barely there.
core.cn: 优雅的纤细，或几乎不存在的差距。

branches.en: A body keeps a fine and easy line.
branches.cn: 身体保持纤细流畅的线条。

branches.en: A win comes by a hair's width.
branches.cn: 胜利只差一根头发那么窄。

branches.en: Fingers and branches stretch long and thin.
branches.cn: 手指和枝条细长伸展。

branches.en: Body and object share the same line.
branches.cn: 身体与物体共享同一种线条。

branches.en: What is thin can still decide an outcome.
branches.cn: 纤细之物也能决定结果。

intro.en: Slender forms words for thinness and narrow margins.
intro.cn: slender 构成表示纤细和微小差距的词。

latinIntro.en: Slender is Middle English, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: slender 是中古英语词，并非拉丁语。

items.example: The vase has a slender neck.
items.exampleCN: 这个花瓶有细长的瓶颈。

items.example: The young tree is more slender.
The slenderness of the tower surprised us.
The dancer has a slender figure.
The dress showed her slender waist.
items.exampleCN: 这条裙子显出她纤细的腰。

items.example: There is a slender chance of snow.
They won by a slender majority.

definition_zh: 鲸；鲸鱼；（口语）巨大的事物、极好的人
definition_en: a very large sea animal that breathes air through a hole on top of its head
core_image: 海面突然升起一股水柱，随后一段黑色的背脊慢慢滑过
scene: 船头的人忽然喊起来，远处海面喷起一道白色水柱，接着一段乌黑的背脊滑过水面。 A whale surfaced beside the boat and blew a tall cloud of spray.
sceneCN: 这里 whale 是「鲸」（第 1 个义项：用头顶喷气孔呼吸的巨大海生动物）；句意为一头鲸在船边浮出水面，喷出高高的一团水雾。海面上腾起的水柱与滑过的黑背脊就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The great sea animal
senses.definition: a huge mammal that lives in the sea, breathes through a blowhole and feeds on small fish or plankton
senses.definitionCN: 生活在海中的巨大哺乳动物，用喷气孔呼吸，以小杂鱼或浮游生物为食
senses.example: A whale surfaced beside the boat and blew a tall cloud of spray.
senses.exampleCN: 一头鲸在船边浮出水面，喷出高高的一团水雾。
senses.why: The meaning of the animal is the only old sense of the word, and everything else in the entry grows out of it.
senses.whyCN: 指这种动物是这个词唯一古老的意思，词条中其余含义都由它长出。

senses.title: A very large example of something
senses.definition: in informal use, something remarkably large of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指同类中极大的东西
senses.example: The new library is a whale of a building.
senses.exampleCN: 新图书馆是一座庞然大物般的建筑。
senses.why: The blue whale is the largest animal that has ever lived, so its name became a measure of sheer size.
senses.whyCN: 蓝鲸是有史以来最大的动物，于是它的名字成了纯粹大小的量尺。

senses.title: A very good person or thing
senses.definition: in phrases such as a whale of a time, someone or something outstanding
senses.definitionCN: 在 a whale of a time 等说法中，指非常出色的人或事
senses.example: The children had a whale of a time at the seaside.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在海边玩得非常尽兴。
senses.why: Great size shades into great quality, so the same animal name praises an experience instead of describing bulk.
senses.whyCN: 极大的体积会滑向极好的品质，于是同一个动物名从形容体量转为称赞体验。

senses.title: To hunt whales
senses.definition: in the verb use, to hunt whales, now usually only in historical or critical text
senses.definitionCN: 动词用法，指捕猎鲸鱼，现多见于历史叙述或批评语境
senses.example: Several nations sailed south to whale in those waters.
senses.exampleCN: 当时有几个国家南下到那片海域捕鲸。
senses.why: English turns a hunted animal into a verb, so whale means the hunt and whaling means the industry.
senses.whyCN: 英语会把被猎的动物变成动词，于是 whale 指捕猎，whaling 指这门行业。

intro.en: Whale comes from Old English hwæl, a word shared with Old Norse and the other Germanic languages, and it has meant this animal and nothing else for over a thousand years.
intro.cn: whale 源自古英语 hwæl，与古诺斯语及其他日耳曼语共有，一千多年来一直指这种动物，别无他义。

items.en: The root probably named the animal by its rolling or blowing look, though the exact picture is lost.
items.cn: 这个词根大概按动物翻滚或喷水的样子来命名，但确切画面已失。

items.en: Hwæl appears in early poetry for the whale as the great fish of the open sea.
items.cn: hwæl 出现在早期诗歌中，指开阔海面上的巨鱼。

items.en: Norse settlers and sailors brought forms such as hvalr, and northern English kept the wh sound.
items.cn: 诺斯定居者与船员带来 hvalr 等形式，英格兰北部保留了 wh 的读音。

items.en: The spelling settled as whal, later whale, and whaling grew into a whole northern industry.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 whal，后作 whale，捕鲸业在北方发展成完整产业。

items.en: The huge size of the animal gave the casual phrases a whale of a time and a whale of a building.
items.cn: 这种动物的巨大体形带来了 a whale of a time、a whale of a building 这类口语说法。

note.en: The first group gathers words that are confused with whale in spelling, the second the sea animals and the words for bigness.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写容易与 whale 相混的词，第二组收海洋动物与表示巨大的说法。

entries.definition: To cry out with a long sad sound, pronounced the same.
entries.definitionCN: 哀号；恸哭，与 whale 同音

entries.definition: A round object that turns, with a different vowel.
During the time that, written almost the same.
The stiff plates from a whale's mouth.
A smaller sea mammal that also breathes through a hole on top.
A large fish with sharp teeth, often confused with the whale in old stories.
The class the whale belongs to, since it feeds its young on milk.
Something enormously large, the idea behind the casual sense.

normalIntro.en: The word is almost a picture of the animal: a wide w for the body, and a long tail of letters after the vowel.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词几乎就是这动物的画像：宽宽的 w 是身体，元音后面拖一条长尾巴。

normal.en: Whale and wail sound the same; one blows water, the other blows noise.
normal.cn: whale 与 wail 同音：一个喷水柱，一个喷哭声。

normal.en: The wh- spelling is old English: who, what, where, whale.
normal.cn: wh- 的拼写很古老：who、what、where、whale 都是。

normal.en: A blue whale is bigger than any dinosaur, which is why its name means huge.
normal.cn: 蓝鲸比任何恐龙都大，所以它的名字才代表巨大。

normal.en: Whaling is the industry, whaler is the ship, whalebone is the material.
normal.cn: whaling 是行业，whaler 是船，whalebone 是材料。

normal.en: A whale of a time means a very good time, not a wet one.
normal.cn: a whale of a time 指非常尽兴，而不是湿淋淋。

abstract.en: Feel the deck shake as something huge passes under it.
abstract.cn: 感觉船甲板在某个巨物从下面经过时发颤。

abstract.en: See a white column stand still in the air for a moment.
abstract.cn: 看一根白色水柱在空中短暂地立住。

abstract.en: Hear a low sound travel a long way through water.
abstract.cn: 听一个低沉的声音在水里传出很远。

examples.en: Whales come to these waters every winter to feed.
examples.cn: 每年冬天鲸都会到这片海域来觅食。

examples.en: People once hunted the animal for its oil, so whaling was a hard trade.
examples.cn: 人们曾为取油而捕杀这种动物，因此捕鲸是一桩艰苦的行当。

examples.en: We had a whale of a time at your party.
examples.cn: 我们在你的聚会上玩得非常尽兴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂了」——喂了它一桶小鱼，鲸就浮上来喷了一道水柱。

root: 古英语 hwæl（鲸）→ 中古英语 whal → whale；与古诺斯语 hvalr 同源，同族有 whaling、whaler、whalebone。

sensesIntro.en: The word names the animal first, then its enormous size turns into a casual word for anything huge, then into praise, and the verb names the hunt.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指这种动物，接着它巨大的体型变成了指任何庞然大物的口语，再变成赞语，最后动词形式指捕猎。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white column of spray over a black back.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑色背脊上方一道白色水柱。

branches.en: The animal branch: a whale surfacing beside the boat.
branches.cn: 动物分支：船边浮出的鲸。

branches.en: The size branch: a whale of a building.
branches.cn: 体量分支：庞然大物般的建筑。

branches.en: The praise branch: a whale of a time at the party.
branches.cn: 赞语分支：聚会上玩得尽兴。

branches.en: The hunting branch: nations sailing south to whale.
branches.cn: 捕猎分支：各国南下捕鲸。

branches.en: The naming branch: whalebone and whale watching built on the animal itself.
branches.cn: 命名分支：鲸须与观鲸都建立在动物本身之上。

intro.en: Whale is a simple Germanic noun, and the family grows through -ing, -er and the compound ending -bone.
intro.cn: whale 是简单的日耳曼语名词，词族靠 -ing、-er 以及复合词尾 -bone 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin named the animal cetus or ballaena; the second of these passed through Greek into scientific words, so the Latin entries below are cognate labels rather than ancestors of whale.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 cetus 或 ballaena 指鲸；后者经由希腊语进入科学术语，所以下面的拉丁条目只是同类标签，并非 whale 的祖先。

items.example: It is both a noun and a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它既可作名词也可作动词。

items.example: It is the earliest recorded shape.
items.exampleCN: 它是最早有记录的词形。

items.meaning: a person or ship that does
the stiff plates of the mouth

items.example: It is a modern tourist phrase.
It carries the size sense into praise.
items.exampleCN: 它把体量义带进赞语里。

definition_zh: 飞机；（乘）飞机这一交通方式
definition_en: a powered flying vehicle with fixed wings, or travel by such a vehicle
core_image: 一架银色的固定翼飞机掠过云层，机翼在光里微微发亮
scene: 机场外的草地上，一个孩子仰头看天，手指跟着那道白线移动。 A small airplane climbed slowly above the trees.
sceneCN: 这里 airplane 是「飞机」（第 1 个义项：有固定机翼的动力飞行器）；句意为一架小飞机缓缓爬升到树梢之上。图中可辨识物件：草地、白线、机翼。

derivatives.zh: 由本词与 mode 合成的名词，义为「飞行模式」
本词的缩略形式，义为「飞机」

senses.title: A fixed-wing flying machine
senses.definition: a powered flying vehicle with fixed wings and an engine, the usual American term
senses.definitionCN: 有固定机翼与发动机的动力飞行器，美式英语的常用说法
senses.example: A small airplane climbed slowly above the trees.
senses.exampleCN: 一架小飞机缓缓爬升到树梢之上。
senses.why: Airplane is a transparent compound of air and plane, where plane is the old word for a flat surface, because the wings are flat.
senses.whyCN: airplane 是 air 与 plane 的透明复合词，而 plane 本指平面，因为机翼是平的。

senses.title: Air travel as a means
senses.definition: in phrases such as by airplane, the means of travelling by air rather than a particular machine
senses.definitionCN: 在 by airplane 这类说法中，指乘飞机这一交通方式，而不是某一架具体的飞机
senses.example: The team travels by airplane when the distance is too long for a bus.
senses.exampleCN: 距离太远、坐大巴不合适时，这支队伍就乘飞机。
senses.why: When the word follows by, it names a mode rather than an object, the same shift that turns bicycle into a way of travelling.
senses.whyCN: 跟在 by 后面时，它命名的是一种方式而非一件物体，这与 bicycle 变成一种出行方式的变化相同。

intro.en: Airplane is an American compound: air plus plane, the old word for a flat surface, named for the flat wings.
intro.cn: airplane 是美式复合词：air 加上 plane，而 plane 本指平面，得名于平坦的机翼。

items.en: Planum meant 'a flat surface', from planus 'flat', the source of plain and plane.
items.cn: planum 意为「平面」，出自 planus「平的」，plain 与 plane 都源于此。

items.en: English plane named a flat surface and a woodworking tool, and later one surface of a wing.
items.cn: 英语 plane 指平面与木工刨，后来也指机翼的一面。

items.en: Early aviation writing used aeroplane in Britain and airplane in America, both built on the flat-wing idea.
items.cn: 早期航空文献在英国用 aeroplane、在美国用 airplane，两者都建立在「平翼」这个想法上。

items.en: Airplane became standard American usage, while aeroplane remained British.
items.cn: airplane 成为美式标准，aeroplane 则留在英式英语中。

items.en: The clipped form plane is now common everywhere, and airplane mode keeps the full word in daily use.
items.cn: 缩略形式 plane 如今各地通用，而 airplane mode 让完整形式仍活跃在日常里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the plane family and its spelling rivals; the near-meaning group gathers flying machines by type.
note.cn: 形近组收 plane 词族与拼写上的对手；近义组收按类型区分的飞行器。

entries.definition: The British spelling and pronunciation of the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的英式拼写与读音。

entries.definition: The short everyday word for an airplane, or a flat surface.
entries.definitionCN: 飞机的日常简称，或指平面。

entries.definition: Simple, ordinary, or a flat stretch of land.
entries.definitionCN: 朴素的、普通的，或指平原。

entries.definition: Any flying machine, including helicopters and balloons.
entries.definitionCN: 任何飞行器，包括直升机与气球。

entries.definition: An aircraft driven by jet engines, usually fast and large.
entries.definitionCN: 由喷气发动机驱动的飞机，通常又快又大。

entries.definition: A plane with no engine that rides rising air.
entries.definitionCN: 没有发动机、借上升气流飞行的飞机。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: air and plane, the flat surface of a wing.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：air 与 plane，也就是机翼的平面。

normal.en: Plane is a flat surface, and a wing is flat: airplane is literally a flat thing in the air.
normal.cn: plane 是平面，而机翼是平的：airplane 字面上就是「空中的平面」。

normal.en: Britain keeps aeroplane, America uses airplane; the aero- part points to air as well.
normal.cn: 英国保留 aeroplane，美国用 airplane；aero- 这个成分同样指向空气。

normal.en: Airplane mode switches the radio off, not the plane.
normal.cn: airplane mode 关掉的是无线电，不是飞机。

normal.en: The verb is not used: you do not airplane somewhere, you fly there.
normal.cn: 这个词不作动词：不能说 airplane 到某地，要说 fly。

normal.en: Plane, plain and plane again: only airplane always means the machine.
normal.cn: plane、plain、plane 容易混：只有 airplane 始终指机器。

abstract.en: Naming a machine after a flat surface shows how concrete the roots of technology words usually are.
abstract.cn: 用平面来命名机器，说明技术词根通常多么具体。

abstract.en: Two spellings for one object record two histories of the same invention.
abstract.cn: 同一个物体有两种拼写，记录了同一项发明的两段历史。

abstract.en: By airplane names a way of travelling, which is why it needs no article.
abstract.cn: by airplane 命名的是一种出行方式，所以不需要冠词。

examples.en: A small airplane climbed slowly above the trees.
examples.cn: 一架小飞机缓缓爬升到树梢之上。

examples.en: The team travels by airplane when the distance is too long for a bus.
examples.cn: 距离太远、坐大巴不合适时，这支队伍就乘飞机。

examples.en: He folded the letter into an airplane and threw it across the room.
examples.cn: 他把信折成一架飞机，扔过整个房间。

sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都出自同一台机器：机器本身，以及这台机器所实现的出行方式。

definition_en: an interjection used to show surprise, to acknowledge that one understands, to hesitate while thinking, or to call someone's attention
core_image: 一个人听到意外消息，嘴巴微张，一声短促的气从喉咙里出来
scene: 深夜的实验室只亮着一盏台灯，学生盯着刚打印出来的曲线，数据和预想的完全相反。 Oh, that cannot be right.
sceneCN: 这里的 oh 表示惊讶（第 1 个义项：吃惊、意外）；句意为「哦，这不可能对吧」，说话人不敢相信眼前的结果。图中可辨识物件：台灯、打印纸、曲线。

pos.zh: 感叹词：表示惊讶、领会、迟疑或招呼

derivatives.zh: 由 oh 拉长元音并加写一个字母而来，语气更夸张，义为「哟；哎呀」
由 oh 重复并以连字符连接而成，用来表示「糟了、要出事」
由 oh 与 so 用连字符复合而成，口语里表示「极其、非常」，常带调侃

senses.title: Surprise or sudden emotion
senses.definition: used to express surprise, shock or a sudden strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 用来表达惊讶、震动或突然涌起的强烈情绪
senses.example: Oh, I did not expect to see you here.
senses.exampleCN: 哦，我没想到会在这儿见到你。
senses.why: A short open vowel burst is the body's first reaction to something unexpected, and English fixed that sound as the word oh.
senses.whyCN: 短促张开的一声元音，是身体遇到意外时最直接的反应，英语就把这个声音固定成了 oh。

senses.title: Acknowledging that one understands
senses.definition: used as a short reply to show that the speaker has heard and understood
senses.definitionCN: 用作简短应答，表示说话人听到了并且明白了
senses.example: Oh, I see what you mean now.
senses.exampleCN: 哦，我现在明白你的意思了。
senses.why: Once the same sound answers another person, it stops being pure feeling and becomes a signal that the message has landed.
senses.whyCN: 同一个声音一旦用来回应别人，就不再只是纯粹的情绪，而成了「话已经接收到」的信号。

senses.title: Hesitating while thinking
senses.definition: used, often lengthened, to hold the floor while the speaker searches for words
senses.definitionCN: 常用拖长的形式，在说话人找词时占住发言的位置
senses.example: Oh, let me think for a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 哦，让我想一会儿。
senses.why: Drawing the sound out fills the silence, so oh turns into a small tool for keeping one's turn in a conversation.
senses.whyCN: 把声音拉长就填满了停顿，于是 oh 变成一个小工具，用来在对话里保住自己这一轮。

senses.title: Calling attention or adding emphasis
senses.definition: used before a name or remark to draw attention or to make the statement more emphatic
senses.definitionCN: 放在名字或话语前，用来引起注意或让语气更重
senses.example: Oh, Tom, the post has come.
senses.exampleCN: 哦，汤姆，邮件到了。
senses.why: The same cry that reacts to the world can be turned outward to reach another person, and there it works as a call.
senses.whyCN: 那声原本对世界作出反应的声音，也可以转向外去够到另一个人，这时它就起招呼的作用。

intro.en: Oh belongs to the small set of English exclamations that seem to come from the voice itself, and its exact origin is uncertain; what is recorded is its long life in speech and writing.
intro.cn: oh 属于英语中少数仿佛直接出自人声的感叹词，确切来源不确定；可考的是它在口语与书面语中长期存在。

items.en: A word of this kind is generally treated as a natural cry rather than a borrowing, so its earliest source is uncertain and no Latin parent can be named.
items.cn: 这类词一般认为属于人自然而发的叫声，而不是从某处借来，因此最早来源不确定，也指不出拉丁语祖先。

items.en: The interjection appears in early English writing as o or oo, used to call out, to mourn or to mark surprise.
items.cn: 这一感叹词在早期英语文献中写作 o 或 oo，用来呼唤、哀叹或表示惊讶。

items.en: By the sixteenth century oh was a common spelling, and it filled the stage with sighs, warnings and sudden turns of plot.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，oh 已是常见拼写，舞台上用它来叹气、示警或表示情节骤转。

items.en: Because the tone carries the meaning, the same oh can mark surprise, understanding, hesitation or distress without changing its shape.
items.cn: 因为意义由语调承载，同一个 oh 能表示惊讶、领会、迟疑或痛苦，而词形不变。

items.en: Modern English keeps oh for speech, letters and fiction, where it stands in for a sound rather than for a thing.
items.cn: 现代英语把 oh 留在口语、书信与小说里，它代替的是一个声音，而不是一件东西。

note.en: The look-alike group collects other short exclamations that look or sound close to oh; the near-meaning group collects interjections with overlapping emotional jobs.
note.cn: 形近组收其他拼写或发音与 oh 接近的短感叹词；近义组收情绪功能与之重叠的感叹词。

entries.definition: A lengthened cry of surprise or delight, close in shape to oh.
entries.definitionCN: 拉长的一声惊呼或欢喜之声，形态与 oh 接近。

entries.definition: A short open cry of relief, pain or surprise.
entries.definitionCN: 表示宽慰、疼痛或惊讶的短促开口声。

entries.definition: A two-part cry marking sudden understanding.
entries.definitionCN: 由两部分组成、表示突然明白的出声。

entries.definition: An exclamation of surprise and admiration.
entries.definitionCN: 表示惊讶与赞叹的感叹词。

entries.definition: An old word expressing sorrow or regret.
entries.definitionCN: 表达悲伤或遗憾的古老感叹词。

entries.definition: A call used to attract attention or to greet.
entries.definitionCN: 用来引起注意或打招呼的招呼声。

normalIntro.en: Oh has no root to dig into; it is a sound that English wrote down, so the hooks follow the voice rather than a word family.
normalIntro.cn: oh 没有可挖掘的词根；它是英语记录下来的一个声音，所以记忆钩子顺着人声走，而不是顺着词族走。

normal.en: Oh has no parts and takes no endings, which places it outside the grammar of nouns and verbs.
normal.cn: oh 没有构件，也不接词尾，这使它落在名词与动词的语法之外。

normal.en: The voice decides the meaning: a rising oh asks, a flat oh acknowledges, a long oh hesitates.
normal.cn: 语调决定意思：上扬的 oh 在追问，平直的 oh 在应答，拖长的 oh 在迟疑。

normal.en: Oh dear and oh no borrow the sound for worry, while oh well borrows it for acceptance.
normal.cn: oh dear 与 oh no 借这个声音表示担忧，oh well 则借它表示接受。

normal.en: In writing, the comma after oh marks a pause that the voice would make anyway.
normal.cn: 书写时 oh 后面的逗号，标出的是人声本来就会有的停顿。

normal.en: Oh before a name turns the cry outward, which is why it can open a sentence addressed to someone.
normal.cn: oh 放在名字前，就把这声叫喊转向外，所以它能开启一句对某人说的话。

abstract.en: A word that is only a sound reminds us that language begins in breath before it settles into spelling.
abstract.cn: 一个只是声音的词提醒人：语言在落成拼写之前，先起于呼吸。

abstract.en: Oh can be surprise, agreement or delay because the listener reads the tone, not the letters.
abstract.cn: oh 能表示惊讶、同意或拖延，是因为听者读的是语调，不是字母。

abstract.en: Every conversation leaves a few of these small openings where feeling shows through.
abstract.cn: 每场对话都会留下几处这样的小缺口，情绪从中露出来。

examples.en: Oh, the train was delayed again.
examples.cn: 哦，火车又晚点了。

examples.en: Oh, now I understand the whole plan.
examples.cn: 哦，我现在明白整个计划了。

examples.en: Oh, mind the step at the door.
examples.cn: 哦，当心门口的台阶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧」——张嘴一声「欧」，惊讶、明白都靠它；记住 oh 是感叹词。

root: 来源不确定；一般认为这类感叹词由人自然发出的声音固定而成，与任何拉丁词根都没有派生关系。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an open-mouthed sound of reaction; it branches into surprise, the reply that shows understanding, the drawn-out pause, and the call aimed at another person.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是遇事张口发出的一声；由此分出惊讶、表示明白的应答、拖长的停顿，以及冲着别人发出的招呼。

core.cn: 核心意象：一个人听到意外消息，嘴巴微张，一声短促的气从喉咙里出来。

definition_en: the duty to explain one's actions and accept responsibility for them
core_image: 听证席上，一叠预算文件被推到发言人面前
scene: 听证会上，官员被要求逐项说明预算的去向。 Voters demanded greater accountability from the council.
sceneCN: 这里的 accountability 指「问责」（第 1 个义项：必须对行为作出交代并接受监督）；句意是选民要求市政会接受更严格的问责。

senses.title: Being answerable to others
senses.definition: the state of being required to explain decisions to a public or an authority
senses.definitionCN: 必须向公众或上级说明决定的状态
senses.example: Voters demanded greater accountability from the council.
senses.exampleCN: 选民要求市政会接受更严格的问责。
senses.why: The noun is built on accountable, whose root is the counting of money; being made to count out one's decisions is the institutional sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词建立在 accountable 之上，词根是数钱记账；被要求把自己的决定一笔笔交代清楚，就是制度层面的问责。

senses.title: Taking responsibility oneself
senses.definition: a personal readiness to own the results of one's own actions
senses.definitionCN: 个人愿意为自己行为的结果负责
senses.example: She showed real accountability for the mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这个错误表现出真正的担当。
senses.why: The same duty can be worn from inside rather than imposed from outside, and that inner readiness is this second sense.
senses.whyCN: 同一份责任可以由外强加，也可以由内承担，这种主动承担就是第二个义项。

intro.en: The word is accountable with a suffix that names a quality, and it grows out of the counting of money.
intro.cn: 这个词是 accountable 加表示性质的后缀，源头是数钱记账。

items.en: computare meant to count up.
items.cn: computare 意为结算。

items.en: aconter meant to render a reckoning.
items.cn: aconter 意为作出交代。

items.en: account named the reckoning itself.
items.cn: account 指结算这件事。

items.en: accountable described a person who must answer for money held.
items.cn: accountable 描述必须为经手钱款作出交代的人。

items.en: accountability widened from money to power, promises and mistakes.
items.cn: accountability 从钱款扩展到权力、承诺与过失。

note.en: The look-alike group is the account family; the near-meaning group names responsibility and openness.
note.cn: 形近组是 account 词族；近义组表示责任与公开。

dict_mnemonic.text: account（交代账目）+ -able（能……的）+ -ity（性质）——必须把账交代清楚的性质，就是问责。
